title: Experiment 10 – Dijkstra's Shortest Path Routing Algorithm
description: Implementation of Dijkstra's algorithm in C to compute single-source shortest path routing tables for Link State Routing (OSPF).
aim: To implement Dijkstra's shortest path routing algorithm in C to find minimum cost routes in a computer network.
theory: Dijkstra's algorithm is a greedy algorithm used in Link-State routing protocols like OSPF and IS-IS to compute the Shortest Path Tree (SPT) from a single source router to all other network routers. Each router maintains a global link-state database (LSDB), and through edge relaxation, computes the optimal routing table.
algorithm: Initialize distance array: dist[source] = 0, and dist[i] = cost[source][i] for all other nodes.
Mark source as visited in visited[] array and set parent pointers.
Find unvisited node u with minimum distance value.
Update distances of all unvisited neighbors v: if dist[u] + cost[u][v] < dist[v], then dist[v] = dist[u] + cost[u][v] and parent[v] = u.
Repeat until all nodes are visited or minimum distance is infinity.
Print routing table displaying destination, minimum cost, and complete node path.
